title: Replacing a project with an unfinished wire blanks the entire application
area: Workspace pending terminal state; project load/new/import transitions
steps: 1. Open the heating starter. 2. Click PS-01 positive terminal once, leaving the wire preview active. 3. Click New empty experiment.
expected: A usable empty canvas; all transient wire and selection state cleared.
actual: The root UI disappears. An uncaught exception says “Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'kind')”. Reloading the page is required.
evidence: edge-observations.json: pending-wire-crash and pageerror; 21-pending-wire-crash.png. Also encountered independently during the first electrical construction session.
impact: A routine construction transition loses the working interface and exposes unsaved work to loss.
cause: Hypothesis, supported by local source: Workspace holds pending in component state and dereferences a component from the replacement project using a non-null assertion (src/components/Workspace.tsx, pending preview). The local source is not proven identical to the remote build.
fix: Clear project-bound transient editor state whenever project identity changes; guard lookup before rendering pending previews; add a recoverable application error boundary.
accept: New, challenge switch and import while a wire is pending never throw; the replacement project renders; no terminal from the previous project remains pending. Recovery UI can preserve/export valid project state after an unexpected render exception.
tests: Browser tests for pending wire followed by New, valid import, challenge start and device recovery; assert no pageerror, visible canvas and cleared preview.

title: Failed electrical solves retain apparently valid live readings
area: Electrical solve failure, inspector, canvas, probes, measurement tool and CSV
steps: 1. Import audit-evidence/E01.physics.json (12 V, 6 Ω). 2. Add a wire junction. 3. Wire source positive to the junction and the junction to source negative. 4. Inspect the resistor and source.
expected: The short is rejected with actionable diagnostics; quantities for the invalid circuit display unavailable or explicitly last-valid with a timestamp.
actual: The correct short-circuit diagnostic appears and running is prevented, but the read API retains 12 V, 2 A and 24 W with voltageValid=true from the old solution. The canvas still shows those values, and the selected junction shows HEALTHY / 12.00 V. Follow-up confirmed that the resistor inspector's detailed electrical rows already show unavailable values; invalidation is inconsistent across surfaces.
evidence: extended-observations.json: E05-real-short, E05-real-short-ui, E05-run; 07-real-short.png; E05-short.physics.json. Follow-up evidence: performance-observations.json and 25-stale-short.png when present.
impact: An engineer can mistake an obsolete solution for the result of the displayed topology. Zero residual values also cease to mean a successful current solve.
cause: Hypothesis: the failure path stores an error while leaving the previous electrical result and validity flags intact.
fix: Attach solution status and revision to calculated outputs. Invalidate dependent readings on failure and propagate that validity through every presentation/export route; preserve last-valid data only behind an explicit label.
accept: For a shorted source no current-solution electrical numeric value is shown as valid. Diagnostic names PS-01 and the remedy. Undo restores the original 2 A / 24 W solution without reload.
tests: Browser and engine tests: valid circuit → short → failed solve → inspector/probes/tool/CSV validity → undo → valid solve. Also test conflicting ideal sources.

title: The supplied HTTPS entry point does not serve TLS
steps: Navigate to https://fracht.lennartobst.de:8080 in Chromium, or run curl -I against that exact URL.
expected: A successful HTTPS application response, or a documented working HTTPS canonical URL.
actual: Chromium reports net::ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR; curl reports TLS wrong version number. http://fracht.lennartobst.de:8080 returns HTTP 200 and serves the working app.
evidence: access-checks.txt; remote-index.html. Browser 156.0.8078.4 reproduced the exact HTTPS error before HTTP testing.
impact: The advertised entry point is inaccessible. The HTTP fallback was necessary to conduct this audit.
cause: Hypothesis: the listener on port 8080 serves plaintext HTTP rather than TLS.
fix: Provide TLS termination at the intended public entry point and align shared links with the canonical deployment URL. Verify static assets under that origin.
accept: The exact supplied HTTPS URL loads the application with a browser-trusted certificate and successful JS/CSS requests; any canonical redirect remains HTTPS.
tests: External deployment smoke test using certificate validation and a real Chromium navigation; verify the application canvas and asset status codes.

title: Click-to-add overlaps components and obstructs selection
area: Library click placement and schematic layout
steps: 1. Create a new empty experiment. 2. Click DC power supply in the library. 3. Click Resistor. 4. Try selecting the source at its center.
expected: Both newly inserted components remain individually accessible; placement avoids existing component footprints.
actual: At 1600×1000, source transform is translate(320,240), resistor translate(280,240); their bodies substantially overlap. In the earlier session the resistor intercepted the attempted source click. Drag placement provided a working workaround.
evidence: edge-observations.json: click-placement; 22-click-overlap.png; electrical-blocked.png from the initial exploratory session.
impact: The documented simple click workflow immediately creates cleanup work and obscures terminals and labels.
cause: Hypothesis: placement offsets vary with component count without testing existing bounds.
fix: Find an unoccupied snapped component footprint near the visible canvas center, or enter a clear placement mode after a library click.
accept: Click-add ten mixed components into an empty viewport without overlapping selectable bodies; all remain selectable or are included by Fit experiment. Manual drag placement still works.
tests: Browser layout test comparing component bounding rectangles after repeated click additions, with rotation and non-default zoom.

title: Mobile telemetry labels and controls overlap
steps: 1. Open the heating starter. 2. Add a differential node-voltage trace from source negative to heater positive. 3. Run/advance two seconds. 4. Set viewport to 390×844.
expected: Trace names, numerical values, units, history and trace controls occupy separate readable areas.
actual: History timestamp/readouts and trace labels visibly overprint each other near the top of the telemetry panel. Body scrollWidth remains 390 px, so an overflow-only test misses the defect.
impact: Users cannot reliably associate a value with its signal on a small screen.
cause: Hypothesis: desktop flex/absolute layout retains incompatible widths at the mobile breakpoint.
fix: Stack telemetry metadata and controls; wrap trace readouts into distinct rows with stable label/value/unit columns. Offer a taller or collapsible chart panel.
accept: At 390×844 and 360×800, three mixed-unit traces have non-overlapping labels, values and controls; keyboard focus remains visible; no horizontal page overflow.
tests: Responsive browser tests asserting disjoint relevant DOM bounding boxes, plus reviewed screenshots at both sizes. Include longer user trace names.

title: Permanent starter and assembly controls crowd out the component catalog
steps: Open the default workspace at 1600×1000 and inspect the library. Browse the Electrical group without search.
expected: The primary catalog has enough space to browse several component options without repeated scrolling.
actual: The library scroll area is about 241.6 px high while the permanent starter/assembly tools consume 318 px. Only roughly three standard catalog rows are initially visible below the category heading.
impact: Discovering 39 catalog entries requires disproportionate scrolling. Starter shortcuts dominate the construction tool they are meant to support.
cause: Hypothesis: all starter buttons and assembly tools sit in a fixed non-scrolling footer.
fix: Move starters into an Experiments menu or collapsible region and collapse assembly authoring until selected. Give the catalog the remaining vertical space.
accept: At 1600×1000 the collapsed default library allocates at least 450 px to the catalog; every starter remains reachable within two clicks and keyboard navigation.
tests: Browser layout assertions at 1600×1000 and 1280×720; smoke-test starter navigation and saved assembly insertion after rearrangement.

title: Timer event timestamps precede the configured delay by one fixed step
area: Automation transition logging and time semantics
steps: Import timer-1.physics.json: a 20°C tank sensor drives a true <80 comparator and a TON timer with delay=1 s. Run at 0.25×, 1× and 4× and inspect Event log.
expected: The log clearly associates the 1 s TON transition with its effective simulation-time boundary.
actual: All three runs log TM-01: ON at 00:00:00.98. This is speed-independent, but about 1/60 s before the nominal threshold. No claim is made here that the physical output itself triggers early: the exposed measurement tool does not return timer memory.
impact: Users comparing protection timing against specification see an apparent premature transition.
cause: Hypothesis supported by local source: automation consumes dt and logs at the step-start time before the engine increments time.
fix: Define start/end-of-step event semantics and timestamp interval-completion transitions at the effective boundary. Use integer ticks or explicit tolerances for duration thresholds.
accept: A timer asserted at t=0 with a 1 s delay logs its effective transition at t=1 s within floating-point tolerance, consistently across speeds; no fixed step is counted twice.
tests: Single-step timer tests checking the output before and after tick 60, exact event time, reset, TOF and pulse behavior; browser speed comparison.

title: Technical identifiers and very small canvas text weaken measurement readability
area: Inspector measurement names, schematic captions and reference consistency
steps: Inspect a water tank and heater in the default 78% fitted workspace.
expected: Human-readable measurement labels and legible engineering values with clear branch semantics.
actual: The inspector exposes identifiers such as fluidTemperature, transferredVolume and massResidual. Ordinary resistor/heater/source currents share the relay-oriented label “NO / branch current”. Small canvas annotations are difficult to read in the default fitted view.
evidence: 01-initial.png; observations.json: initial-text and heater-fields; verification-observations.json: desktop-ui-metrics. This is a readability review, not a measured contrast-compliance failure.
impact: Users must translate internal identifiers and infer irrelevant contact terminology while interpreting results.
cause: Hypothesis: labels fall back to measurement identifiers and a shared relay-current string.
fix: Create contextual display labels and descriptions for every measurement. Keep identifiers in exports only when accompanied by a schema. Prioritize readable values when fit zoom shrinks symbols.
accept: Tank properties read “Fluid temperature”, “Transferred volume” and “Mass balance residual”; current labels distinguish source, passive branch, motor armature/bus and relay NO/NC. Primary values remain readable at default fit.
tests: Label mapping tests for component families and browser screenshots at desktop default fit and 200% browser zoom. Do not infer full accessibility compliance from those tests.

title: Voltmeter inspector headlines temperature instead of measured voltage
area: Inspector primary reading selection for meter components
steps: Import audit-evidence/E02-meter.physics.json and select VM-01. The 10 MΩ meter is wired across one 6 Ω resistor in a 12 V series circuit.
expected: The primary instrument reading is approximately 5.9999982 V, labeled as differential terminal voltage. Any modeled meter temperature is secondary.
actual: The inspector headlines 20.00°C and Thermal state. The actual 6.000 V reading appears only in the smaller measurement list.
impact: The instrument's most prominent value communicates the wrong physical quantity even though its underlying electrical calculation is correct.
cause: Hypothesis supported by local Inspector source: isThermalMass takes precedence in primary-reading selection, and the voltmeter inherits passive thermal mass.
fix: Choose primary measurement by component purpose: meter voltage first, with explicit differential reference semantics; keep temperature in auxiliary telemetry.
accept: Selecting VM-01 in the fixture prominently shows 6.00 V rather than 20.00°C. Open/floating/invalid conditions display unavailable voltage with a clear reason. Meter thermal accounting remains unchanged.
tests: Browser tests for meter primary value/unit under a known divider, open input and failed circuit; retain engine loading test with 10 MΩ input.
